# A round run moves its base while it runs, so its clean tree is not on a remote tip and the release keeps it. A second, fresh run of the
# same round item moves the clean kept tree to the new tip of origin/<base>, detached.
isolate

exec git init -q -b main origin
exec git -C origin add readme.txt
exec git -C origin -c user.name=e2e -c user.email=e2e@example.com commit -q -m start
exec git -C origin checkout -q -b integration/r1
exec git -C origin add BASE_MARKER
exec git -C origin -c user.name=e2e -c user.email=e2e@example.com commit -q -m base
exec git -C origin checkout -q main

fixture project.star config/projects/local.star
replace config/projects/local.star '~/work/your-repo' $WORK/origin
subst flow/round.star
chmod 755 move-base.sh

exec beehavereal item add local round/integration/r1 --title 'The round' --body-file body.txt
exec beehavereal run round/integration/r1 local --workflow flow/round.star
stdout 'item round/integration/r1 finished'
exists state/trees/local/round_2Fintegration_2Fr1
exec cat run.head
cp stdout first
exec git -C origin rev-parse integration/r1
cp stdout tip
! cmp first tip

exec beehavereal run round/integration/r1 local --workflow flow/round.star
stdout 'item round/integration/r1 finished'
exec cat run.head
cmp stdout tip
exec git -C state/trees/local/round_2Fintegration_2Fr1 rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
stdout '^HEAD$'

-- body.txt --
The round of the base.
-- origin/readme.txt --
The source repository.
-- origin/BASE_MARKER --
base marker
-- move-base.sh --
#!/bin/sh
# The first run moves the base on the remote; a later run finds the mark and moves nothing.
[ -e "$1/moved" ] && exit 0
touch "$1/moved"
cd "$1/origin" || exit 1
git checkout -q integration/r1
git -c user.name=e2e -c user.email=e2e@example.com commit -q --allow-empty -m moved
git checkout -q main
-- flow/round.star --
def main(item):
    command(name = "work", run = ["sh", "-c", "git rev-parse HEAD > @WORK@/run.head; sh @WORK@/move-base.sh @WORK@"])
